newsitem.title: USA: Safety-Kleen sees 1996 revs at $920 million.
newsitem.headline: Safety-Kleen sees 1996 revs at $920 million.

text.p: Safety-Kleen Corp said Thursday it expected revenues for its current year to reach about $920 million and saw revenues through 1999 growing at a annual compound rate of about 11 percent.
Improved revenue growth is expected to be generated by a new vacuum-service business, expansion of its oil-recovery business and continued growth in its industrial services business, it said.
Safety-Kleen provides services for the recovery and recycling of waste fluids.
Safety-Kleen introduced its vacuum-service business at a company-sponsored conference Thursday.

The service is designed to be used by automotive and small industrial shops with oil-water separators that must be cleaned of residual oil and sludge on a regular basis. Safety-Kleen is adding a new fleet of specialized trucks for the service.
The company said it expected the business to renew growth in its traditional automotive markets.
By the end of the year, the company expects to offer the vaccum service in a third of its branches in the U.S., said John Johnson Jr, Safety-Kleen's president, in remarks prepared for the conference.

"Our larger customers have asked Safety-Kleen to provide this service nationally, and we plan to achieve this," he said. "We believe the vacuum service will grow to over $50 million of annual revenues over the next three years."

Johnson cautioned that there are many factors that might cause actual results to differ from the company's revenue projections. Those include the adoption of new environmental laws and regulations, and changes in the way such laws and regulations are interpreted and enforced.
